angles.drive: Competing against someone moves you faster than any praise. Since you carry little Metal, you would rather borrow strength from a contest than from comfort. Compete with someone who also wants you to win, because you run a race that never announces a finish.

Being first to bet is the part you enjoy. Betting first gives you strength where waiting gives none, and the bold move comes ahead of the sure one. Let one sure thing count, because you never count wins you did not bet on.

A shared risk is your fastest way into partnership. Being in it together matters more than being safe, and you split the stakes before the roles. Keep the roles clear, because you lose friends in a loose deal as easily as cash.

Your sense of fair is a running score, one column per friend. With more Metal than you use, you count the friends you keep instead of having them. You know already that you count to stay fair and lose the closeness to the score.

A small bet feels like no bet, and a safe one like a loss. The stakes wake you up, and you would rather bet past safe than sit out. Notice that you bet on the thrill from the account that pays the rent.

Losing to a peer follows you home and stays the night. Since your worth runs on comparison, you read every loss as being less rather than doing less. You are allowed to lose a round without losing your place, and forget it each time.

You compete best with someone to beat and know it. Knowing where you stand matters more than comfort, so you compete harder against one rival than for any reward. Pick one contest with a finish line, because you compete with no end in sight.

Your yes to a bet comes before the fear has finished. Hesitating feels like losing to yourself, so you bet first and size it afterwards. Keep one bet a year you can afford to lose, since nerve costs you money as much as pride.

You trust a person faster once the risk is shared. Sharing the risk makes the bond real to you, so you go in together ahead of writing anything down. Write the terms down once, because you risk the friendship as much as the money.

You keep an exact score with everyone you like. With Metal running over, you run on comparison more than company, so you keep a quiet tally of who gave more. Remember that you started counting to be fair and kept counting to be ahead.

Your bets are sized to the thrill ahead of the margin. Metal piles up in you, so your bets run on nerve to spare and caution borrowed. You bet the rent, and you know it, on a feeling that fades faster than the bill.

More than any loss deserves, you hate to lose. You read a loss to a peer as a statement about you, so you argue the result instead of taking it. You hate losing your place, if you are honest, more than losing the point.
